title: Stream Inspector: callsite profiling, per-chunk telemetry, and deterministic scrub rules
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a Stream Inspector feature that attaches lightweight callsite profiling and deterministic log-scrubbing to each output chunk so teams can reason about per-chunk cost, latency, and provenance while satisfying PII/compliance constraints.

Scope:
- Per-chunk metrics: token_count, token_latency_ms, batch_size, kv_cache_hits, model_variant, tool_call_delta (time spent invoking tools). Metrics must be taggable by request_id and chunk_index.
- Spans: create a short-lived tracing span for each chunk generation + an inner span when the runtime issues tool/function calls. Spans should surface callsite file:line for native SDK callers when available.
- Deterministic scrub rules: streaming redaction that ensures identical input sequences yield identical scrubbed outputs across retries and rollbacks (important for audits). Scrub rules must be policy-driven and pluggable (regex + token-aware heuristics).
- Compatibility layer: provide a shim so existing SDKs can opt in without changing existing payload shape; emit new diagnostic fields under X-Stream-Inspector headers only when enabled.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) Streams running with inspector enabled export per-chunk metrics to observability backend (Prometheus histogram + OTLP) without >1% added p95 latency.
2) Traces correlate chunk spans to parent request trace and include deterministic scrub metadata (scrub_version).
3) Scrubbing passes a set of canonical prompt/eval testcases used by Security and Privacy (see test plan).
4) SDK opt-in toggle works in hosted and dedicated modes; no customer-visible change when disabled.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Lightweight spans instead of full per-token tracing to limit overhead and metric cardinality. If teams need token-level debugging they can enable a separate debug mode.
- Deterministic scrubbing uses a two-pass approach: first apply deterministic token-level masking rules, then redact using regex heuristics for non-tokenizable PII. This keeps scrubbing stable across model retokenization changes.
- Per-chunk metrics will be aggregated server-side into sliding windows for dashboards to avoid high cardinality in long lived streams.

Implementation plan:
1) Instrument runtime output path to emit a StreamInspector event per chunk (C++ runtime change + protobuf event schema).
2) Add a sampling/filter layer to avoid flooding OTLP for very high-throughput streams (configurable sample_rate per-project).
3) Implement scrub module in Go shared by hosted/dedicated control planes; expose policy via Console.
4) SDK: small JS/Go/Java wrapper that attaches callsite metadata when available and sets header X-Stream-Inspector: enabled.
5) Dashboard: Grafana panels for per-route chunk latency and callsite heatmaps; link to traces in Tempo.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Stream+Inspector+Design (confluence placeholder)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 (runtime event + span plumbing)
- Scrub rules repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scrub-rules/tree/stream-inspector

acceptance_criteria: Per-chunk metrics exported and visible in Grafana for a sample route within 5 minutes of activation
Chunk spans link to parent request trace and include scrub_version and callsite:file:line when available
Scrubbed streaming logs pass canonical testcases with >= 99% coverage for defined PII categories
SDK opt-in headers set correctly and no visible change to payloads when inspector disabled
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for scrub module with adversarial corpus. 2) Integration test: enable inspector on staging route, stream 10k sessions, assert metrics ingestion and trace correlation. 3) Performance test: compare p50/p95 latency with inspector off vs on at 95th percentile traffic. 4) Regression: verify scrubbing deterministic across retry and replay scenarios.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature flag off by default; enable for internal accounts and infra team (2 days)
Stage 2: enable for low-throughput hosted demo routes with sampling 10% (1 week)
Stage 3: open to broader customers with sampling configurable per-project (2 weeks)
Rollback: feature flag kill-switch and scrub-only mode (no metric emission)
